system_description.narrative_title: Tectonic Flux: War, Energy Shock and Financial Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: Multiple regional wars (Ukraine, the Middle East/Yemen) and elevated great‑power competition are driving cascading risks across energy, shipping and security domains. Those shocks are colliding with a global bond sell‑off, rising yields and volatile markets, while domestic political turbulence (notably Brazil, Spain and France) amplifies policy uncertainty and geopolitical signalling. The system is an open, interdependent process where military escalation, energy chokepoints and financial stressfeed into one another and reshape alliance behaviour, trade flows and technology diffusion.
system_description.scope: Interstate conflicts and alliance dynamics; regional security theatres (Europe, Middle East, Indo‑Pacific); global energy and maritime chokepoints and supply chains; international financial markets and capital flows; strategic technology, arms transfers and defence innovation; domestic political crises and electoral cycles that influence foreign policy.
system_description.super_system: Planetary political‑economic and security order (the globalized economy, international institutional architecture and Earth system that constrain state behaviour).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime chokepoints (oil, diesel, Straits of Hormuz/Bab el‑Mandeb)
International financial markets and sovereign debt/yield dynamics
Regional security theatres (Ukraine/Europe, Middle East/Yemen, Indo‑Pacific tensions)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with sustained Western military and financial backing, are locked in a protracted high-intensity conflict marked by intensified Russian strikes and evolving Ukrainian tactics and weapons that are straining European security and alliance politics.

variables.name: Iran-led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran and its proxy networks (including Houthi forces), Saudi Arabia and other Gulf actors, with intermittent US and international involvement, are engaged in a widening campaign of cross-border strikes and counter‑operations that is broadening regional confrontation dynamics.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China, together with European, Japanese and allied capitals, are accelerating economic and technological decoupling—through tariffs, export controls, industrial policies and corporate reshoring—that is reordering global supply chains and strategic competition.

variables.name: North Korea missile and deterrence flashpoint
variables.description: North Korea, provoking alarm in South Korea, Japan and the United States, is advancing and publicly exercising intermediate‑range and hypersonic missile capabilities, raising the risk of rapid escalation on the Korean peninsula.

variables.name: Global energy and maritime chokepoints
variables.description: Global energy markets, involving major producers, consumer blocs and international shipping, are being disrupted by attacks on tankers, route diversions and coordinated strategic stock releases, producing sustained fuel supply volatility and logistics strain.
